purpose: Evaluate how well the produced writing serves the specific assignment. Review the actual text, not whether a structural checker passed.

criteria.label: Task fit
criteria.description: Does the writing address the requested topic, purpose, and intended audience?

criteria.label: Completeness
criteria.description: Does it contain the important ideas requested, without material omissions?

criteria.label: Clarity
criteria.description: Is it understandable, coherent, and easy to follow?

criteria.label: Style
criteria.description: Does its tone, voice, and presentation fit the user-specified style?

criteria.label: Constraints
criteria.description: Does it honor instructions such as length, format, or prohibited content?

anchors.1: Poor: largely irrelevant or fails critical requirements.
anchors.2: Weak: relevant fragments but major omissions or style/constraint violations.
anchors.3: Adequate: useful draft with several noticeable weaknesses.
anchors.4: Good: meets the assignment with only minor issues.
anchors.5: Excellent: well-matched, polished writing that fully satisfies the visible assignment.

pairwise.instruction: Read both outputs for the same assignment. Compare task fit, completeness, clarity, style, and stated constraints. Do not reward length by itself.
pairwise.tie_rule: Choose tie if neither text is meaningfully better, including when both are poor. Explain the most important consideration.

limitations: Judge only requirements visible in the task. If important context is missing, say so in the reason rather than guessing. Hidden executable checks are not a substitute for reading quality.
